# Repository guidance

## Product scope

This project is a **small, trusted-workspace ACP → A2A gateway**, not a multi-agent
orchestration platform. Keep adapter responsibilities limited to protocol mapping,
single-turn admission, stream/context continuity, cancellation, accurate task
outcomes and owned-resource cleanup. Model reasoning quality is separate from
adapter correctness. Do not add production schedulers, roles, scorers, model
profiles, retries or new dependencies to restore the retired managed lab.

Start with [README](README.md), [architecture](docs/architecture.md),
[pitfalls](docs/pitfalls.md), and [SDK cancellation constraints](docs/sdk-cancellation.md).
The [historical index](docs/history.md) records the retired lab and unresolved
findings; retirement does **not** mean failures have been fixed.

## Safety and test boundaries

- **Never** expose the unauthenticated gateway through a public proxy.
  Workspaces must be explicitly trusted; production inherits OpenCode configuration,
  provider access, tools, plugins and MCP. ACP permission rejection is not a sandbox.
- Use Linux/Bun 1.4.4 with stable OpenCode 2.2.7 or newer (live acceptance recorded on 2.2.7). For MCP interop use the
  verified a2abridge 4.0.2 binary and its endpoint guard with exact peer/tool
  allowlists. No global service/configuration edits.
- Do not publish prompts, credentials, private reasoning, raw provider diagnostics
  or private network reports in logs, issues or pull requests.
- Run `make check` and relevant focused tests. CI also executes
  `make package-smoke` and verified, provider-free `make interop-test`.
  Never silently substitute these for live-model evidence.
- `make demo`, `make e2e`, `bun scripts/acp-smoke.ts` and the
  `tests/live-*.ts` probes require explicit live execution and provider access.
  These are **not** part of ordinary CI.
- The SDK 1.3 cancellation persistence adapter must remain until a pinned,
  published upstream SDK version passes its reproducer and transport regressions.
  Do not replace accurate terminal task states with optimistic cancellation.
- Do not accidentally reintroduce compiled test duplicates in `dist/` to Bun's
  test discovery; keep `bun test ./tests` scoped.

## Optional guarded MCP workflows

For model-issued delegation, the reviewed route is:
**OpenCode coordinator → guarded MCP endpoint → a2abridge → A2A gateway → ACP worker**.
Do not substitute native subagents, direct ACP calls or the A2A CLI when the request
specifically requires this route. The gateway itself is an A2A server, not an MCP
server.

Use [one-worker setup](docs/manual-one-worker.md) for a continuity smoke and the
[full two-worker bootstrap](docs/manual-two-worker-pipeline.md) with
[passive supervision](docs/passive-mcp-supervision.md) for the separately requested
pipeline smoke. For other approved topology investigations, consult the specific
issue and [portable skill](.opencode/skills/multi-a2a-agent/SKILL.md) rather than
inventing a new runner.

Trust exact worker cards/peer URLs; check the actual model-visible tool catalog,
not just network availability. Submit using `blocking:false`, follow up with the
returned `context_id` and **no** old `task_id`, verify stored task artifacts,
and retain actual pending/uncertain outcomes. Each guarded connection has a
40-attempt ceiling and the operator reserves eight calls for intervention.
Use bounded monotonic deadlines and spaced polls; do not resend uncertain tasks
or assume a zero process exit implies task completion.

All smoke infrastructure must be **owned and isolated**: use a fresh private HOME,
then derive XDG variables from that HOME in later shell commands. Verify the
effective OpenCode configuration before starting a private service. Never change
a separate, existing OpenCode service or its state/registration as a diagnostic
side effect. Clean up only owned processes, directory registrations, workspaces and
ports. Do not infer that an unfinished task was canceled.

## Common implementation traps

- Bun HTTP shutdown requires rejecting new work while the bridge closes and
  retaining the listener handle until incomplete HTTP clients are force-drained,
  then explicitly closing the listener; draining connections alone does not close it.
- `prepack` must remove old compiled JS before building; wildcard runtime
  packaging must not include obsolete `dist/src` files.
- A new context uses a new ACP session; continuation must reuse the actual ACP
  session binding and reject stale context IDs rather than restarting silently.
- Timeout and cancellation are different operations: do not label a lost or
  uncertain completion as `canceled`.
- Do not assume cold, standalone OpenCode has registered MCP tools. The manual
  workflow verifies the tools from the **same warmed owned server** before work.
- Treat test names, receipt environment variables and external acceptance
  contracts as consumers when editing fixtures or reducing tests.

For past incidents and detailed investigation evidence, follow the Git-provenance
links in [docs/history.md](docs/history.md) instead of expanding this file into a
chronological incident diary.

## Lessons Learned

- 2026-10-30: Pitfall: Updating negative fixtures can remove independent policy and precedence checks. Prevention: retain original adversarial cases and add overlapping-invalid-input tests; verify each policy mutation makes a targeted assertion fail.
- 2026-10-30: Pitfall: Disposable OpenCode homes can collide on managed-service ports, and a scrubbed `PATH` can hide the pinned executable. Prevention: bind-check and set private service ports, retain pinned binary paths, and run effective-config probes from the disposable project cwd.
- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: GitHub's latest OpenCode release endpoint can select V1 despite newer V2 releases. Prevention: enumerate releases, select the intended major explicitly, and verify the exact tag and downloaded artifact before changing runtime admission.
- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: Bun upgrades changed closeAllConnections from implicitly closing the listener to draining clients only. Prevention: retain the listener through incomplete-client draining, then explicitly close it and verify port rebinding plus unrelated-listener survival.
- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: Fixture startup timeouts during concurrent validation are insufficient evidence of runtime regressions. Prevention: serialize owned timing-sensitive suites and measure startup separately before attributing failures or changing deadlines.
- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: A pre-created local temporary directory hid fixture failures on fresh CI. Prevention: use the platform temporary directory with mkdtemp, and validate fresh-filesystem behavior instead of depending on harness-specific parent directories.
- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: Deadline handling misclassified callback and transport failures as timeouts or aborts. Prevention: classify errors at their originating operation and test misleading error causes.
- 2026-11-11: Pitfall: A launcher reported cleanup after its root exited while a detached child still held a listener. Prevention: establish descendant ownership at launch and verify owned processes and listeners before deleting records.

# Multi-Agent A2A Workflows

Adapt commands, component names, and operational steps to the host project. Keep reusable coordination patterns here; keep concrete instance layouts, endpoints, tool names, versions, budgets, authorization, and run evidence in the host project's runbook.

## Select one topology

Read this common workflow first, then load only the matching reference. These are
procedural templates, not recovered verbatim prompts, executable runners, or evidence
that a particular scale works. Establish and review the instance/edge map before
execution, using the user's requested scope and the host's linked bootstrap recipe;
do not increase a prior experiment's limits.

| Need                                                        | Reference                                                                       | Control                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Forward each completed result to the next stage             | [Pipeline](references/topology-pipeline.md)                                     | Coordinator relays every hop                        |
| Close a bounded relay in the starting worker's context      | [Bounded ring](references/topology-bounded-ring.md)                             | Coordinator relays every hop                        |
| Return an actual critique to the original proposer          | [Propose–critique–revise](references/topology-propose-critique-revise.md)       | Coordinator relays and continues proposer context   |
| Compare independent proposals through a separate judge      | [Competing proposals / judge](references/topology-competing-proposals-judge.md) | Coordinator gathers and forwards original artifacts |
| Collect independent contributions for coordinator synthesis | [Fan-out / fan-in](references/topology-fan-out-fan-in.md)                       | Coordinator dispatches and collects                 |
| Branch a common input, then join separate reviews           | [Diamond](references/topology-diamond.md)                                       | Coordinator preserves branch identities at the join |
| Delegate through parent-child-only peer links               | [Decentralized tree](references/topology-decentralized-tree.md)                 | Worker sessions issue child calls                   |
| Exercise selected peer links without unbounded propagation  | [Decentralized mesh](references/topology-decentralized-mesh.md)                 | Worker sessions issue a finite peer-call wave       |

## Identify the architecture before execution

Establish the actual control and data paths. A common arrangement is:

```text
OpenCode coordinator
  → OpenCode MCP client
  → local MCP server or endpoint guard
  → MCP-to-A2A client/bridge
  → A2A HTTP agent endpoint
  → protocol adapter
  → worker runtime/session
```

The host project may use different names or combine components. Identify which component enforces tool/peer policy, which translates MCP operations to A2A, and which adapts A2A requests to the worker protocol. Treat a discovery directory as control-plane infrastructure unless evidence shows task traffic passes through it.

Before a run, require a topology specification that names:

- Every coordinator, worker, judge, relay, and adapter instance, including its process/session boundary.
- Each directed logical message edge and the exact physical route used to carry it.
- Which model/session issues each MCP call; whether workers can call other workers; and how results return.
- The A2A endpoint and ACP or other worker endpoint associated with each agent instance.
- The guard's permitted tool set and exact peer allowlist for each caller.
- How context IDs, task IDs, artifacts, deadlines, and terminal states are correlated.

Keep concrete topology layouts, endpoint values, and allowlists specific to the host project and run; record them in the project's issue or operational documentation, not in this reusable skill. The linked references describe generic patterns only.

When authorized to provision disposable infrastructure, instantiate the host's
documented minimal example and review the resulting projects/configuration yourself.
"Reviewed" does not mean the user must supply preconfigured projects. Use the host's
explicitly approved non-secret model selection in each private project; creating that
selection does not authorize a new model/provider, copying credentials, or changing
global configuration. An unrelated global model need not be inherited into private HOME.

Do not infer arbitrary nodes, edges, permissions or termination rules from a topology
name alone. If the requested scope has no documented bootstrap/specification, report
that documentation gap. Do not label empty disposable projects or absent local MCP
configuration as blockers when the linked recipe specifies how to create them.

## Prepare and run

1. Read the request, the topology specification, and the host project's operational guidance. Separate model/task goals from adapter acceptance criteria.
2. Prepare and review owned coordinator/worker projects using the host runbook; do not mistake missing disposable setup for a blocker. Review inherited configuration, provider access, worker identities, cards, and exact tool/peer allowlists. Do not expose credentials or modify shared service state.
3. Check free loopback ports before starting anything. Start only owned resources, keep listeners private, and record their PIDs, ports, endpoint URLs, and returned task/context handles privately.
4. Use OpenCode as coordinator when the topology requires model-directed calls. Calls must traverse the configured MCP guard and adapter path; do not silently substitute a host script, direct protocol client, or a different delegation mechanism.
5. Enforce per-operation deadlines, poll spacing, and attempt limits with an independent supervisor. A prompt instruction or whole-process timeout is not equivalent. If limits cannot be supervised, do not submit work.
6. Never automatically retry or resend an uncertain submission, guess a handle, reconnect to evade a budget, or infer remote cancellation from local client shutdown.

Distinguish hard pre-dispatch limits from passive threshold detection. A receipt
watchdog can interrupt and flag an overrun but cannot guarantee that a concurrent
burst was prevented. Reconcile the complete final receipts after writers exit;
do not report its processed prefix as the final attempt count. If the requested
safety gate requires prevention that the existing transport cannot provide, stop
before submission and report that specific unsupported gate.

Before a model prompt, verify the intended agent and connected tools on the actual
server used by that session. Inspect worker readiness separately when workers can
delegate; warming a different inspection server does not warm an ACP-owned server.
A catalog is a readiness signal, not proof that the model called a tool.

Map the following contract to the host's actual tool schema once, then apply it to
every hop, including worker-originated calls:

- Explicitly set the tool's nonblocking submission parameter; do not rely on defaults
  or the word "nonblocking" in prose. Forward the explicit argument requirement in
  child-task instructions and verify the actual worker arguments afterward.
- Bind a returned handle to its exact peer, context and task. Start independent
  workers with fresh contexts. For continuation, use the actual returned context;
  where the adapter requires a new task, omit the prior task ID and verify a new one.
- Wait only through the supported task-observation tool. Require a terminal completed
  task and stored artifact before forwarding it as a result. Retain failed, pending,
  uncertain or unexpected states without inventing success or a replacement task.
- Budget polls and elapsed time independently under the reviewed limits. A smaller
  invented poll cap can exhaust before the deadline; a higher cap cannot extend it.
  Supervise each nested operation and its ancestors, including across connections.
- Preserve artifact text and source attribution. Do not paraphrase, normalize, or
  silently substitute a predecessor's artifact when a downstream worker needs it.

## Verify and report

Inspect actual coordinator and worker sessions, paired MCP call/result records, peer/context/task provenance, worker inputs, terminal task states, stored artifacts, and owned-resource cleanup. A catalog entry, successful CLI exit, or model self-report alone is not acceptance evidence.

Report these layers separately:

- OpenCode readiness and MCP tool exposure.
- Guard and adapter behavior, based on observed calls and results.
- Topology execution and model/task outcome.
- Resource operations and cleanup.

Classify missing or ambiguous evidence as `BLOCKED` or `INCOMPLETE`; do not turn a topology/model failure into an adapter failure or vice versa. Keep prompts, answers, credentials, raw receipts, and provider diagnostics private. Publish only sanitized evidence.

## Clean up

On success, failure, timeout, or interruption, close owned clients and MCP connections; stop owned heartbeats; unregister workers while their directory is still available; then stop owned gateways and directory processes in dependency order. Verify exact owned PIDs and every recorded listener are gone before removing private state. Never stop or reconfigure another owner's process or shared service.

# opencode-a2a-lite

> Expose OpenCode through A2A, with ACP doing the heavy lifting.

[![CI](https://github.com/tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite)](https://github.com/tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite/releases/latest)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
![Platform: Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-linux-lightgrey)
![Runtime: Bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-Bun%201.4.4-black)

A small OpenCode ACP → A2A 1.0 gateway for trusted Linux workspaces: point any A2A
client at it and it drives OpenCode. It uses the official A2A and ACP SDKs: OpenCode
owns coding-session behavior, the gateway translates plain-text tasks, streamed output
and context continuity.

```text
A2A client ──HTTP/SSE──▶ opencode-a2a-lite ──ACP (stdio)──▶ opencode ──▶ trusted workspace
```

**Not included:** HTTP OpenCode adapter, database, orchestrator, retries, sandbox.

> [!WARNING]
> The gateway has no authentication (it binds to `127.0.0.1`) and must **never** be
> exposed through a public proxy. It inherits OpenCode configuration, tools, plugins and MCP. Rejecting ACP
> permission requests is **not** an OS sandbox, and cancellation does not roll back work.

## Quick start

```sh
make install             # frozen Bun lockfile
make check               # format, lint, typecheck, deterministic tests, build
bun src/cli.ts --workspace /absolute/path/to/trusted/workspace --port 0
```

Wait for a JSON stdout record such as `{"ready":true,"url":"http://127.0.0.1:.../"}`,
then in a second terminal use the **actual** URL (default port 41241):

```sh
a2a card get http://127.0.0.1:41241
a2a send -a http://127.0.0.1:41241 "Reply with a short greeting." --stream
a2a send -a http://127.0.0.1:41241 --context-id <returned-context-id> "Follow up"
```

The server runs in the foreground and terminates its owned ACP process group on
SIGINT/SIGTERM.

## Requirements

- Linux, **Bun 1.4.4**, and stable **`opencode` v2.2.7 or newer** on `PATH`
  (live acceptance recorded on 2.2.7).
- An explicitly trusted workspace and reviewed OpenCode provider, model, tools,
  plugins, MCP servers and configuration.
- The separate [official A2A CLI](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-cli)
  (tested with 0.3.1) to talk to the running gateway.

Runtime security and compatibility evidence is tracked for
[Bun](docs/bun-runtime-security.md) and [OpenCode](docs/opencode-runtime-upgrade.md).
Standalone Bun and OpenCode's embedded runtime are separate upgrade boundaries;
historical acceptance results do not establish compatibility of a new pair.

## Usage

```text
opencode-a2a-lite --workspace <path> [--port <0..65535>]
opencode-a2a-lite --help | --version
```

| Option / variable                                                               | Meaning                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--workspace`, `A2A_WORKSPACE`                                                  | Explicitly trusted directory. The env var must be an **absolute** path. No implicit current-directory trust. |
| `--port`, `A2A_PORT`                                                            | Listen port (bound to `127.0.0.1`). Default 41241; `0` requests an OS-assigned port. Flags override env.     |
| `A2A_NAME` (128), `A2A_DESCRIPTION` (1024), `A2A_TAGS` (16 tags, 64 chars each) | Agent card metadata only, **not** access control. Nonblank, control-free.                                    |

Run the compiled server with `A2A_WORKSPACE=/absolute/trusted/path make run`;
use `make dev` for development.

### Package distribution

`@tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite` is released on GitHub (see the release badge above).
**npm registry publication has not been verified**; do not assume these work until
the scope/registry is checked:

```sh
bunx @tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite --workspace .
npx --yes @tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite --workspace .
```

Both runners still require Bun. `make package-smoke` tests an installed tarball,
**not** registry publication. See [distribution and release policy](docs/distribution.md).

## Behavior and limitations

The official A2A SDK owns HTTP JSON-RPC, Agent Cards, task persistence and SSE.
The executor accepts nonempty plain text only; multiple text parts are joined with
newlines. A new conversation omits `contextId`; follow-ups pass the returned
`contextId` **without an old task ID**. Each turn creates a new A2A task while
reusing the ACP session for that context.

- Exactly one prompt is active globally; another request fails busy without a queue.
- Contexts/tasks live in memory. Default context capacity is 100; restarting clears
  them. No durable recovery, multi-tenancy or parallel model execution.
- Only ACP `end_turn` means completed; confirmed `cancelled` means canceled.
  Errors and other stop reasons fail the task without publishing private diagnostics.
- Permission requests are rejected/canceled, not silently approved.
- Defaults: 30-second startup/session allocation, 120-second prompt, 5-second
  cancellation and 5-second ACP shutdown. Failure retires the unhealthy bridge.
- Streaming sends stable artifact IDs and ordered append events. Task states are
  SDK-owned; the small [request-handler adapter](src/request-handler.ts) is retained
  for a documented upstream cancellation persistence defect.

See [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [pitfalls](docs/pitfalls.md) and
[SDK cancellation removal criteria](docs/sdk-cancellation.md).
Full A2A TCK certification, interactive approval, rich media, push notifications
and runtime-selected workspaces are not claimed.

## Multi-agent coordination

The **gateway does not orchestrate other agents**. Optional guarded MCP interoperability
helpers and their independent gate live in [`interop/`](interop/README.md).
The experimental [team examples](examples/teams/README.md) provide a local roster
launcher; read their supervision and cleanup limitations before use.
For a manually owned model-issued MCP → A2A flow use the
[one-worker recipe](docs/manual-one-worker.md), or the

# OpenCode specialist teams

**Experimental, trusted-local use only.** Known limitations: there is no independent supervision of task deadlines, polling or the eight-call reserve (the coordinator prompt asks for them, nothing enforces them), and teardown stops each recorded process and its process group but does not verify that every detached descendant exited.

Start independent OpenCode workers and open a coordinator for their roster. The coordinator reaches them through one guarded MCP-to-A2A bridge. Worker configs stay native to OpenCode.

## Start and use a team

Start every worker profile in a folder with one command.

```bash
make team-up TEAM=examples/teams/research
make team-up TEAM=examples/teams/research MODE=run > answer.md
```

Folder mode starts one worker per `.json` or `.jsonc` file using its filename stem as the worker name. It skips `coordinator.json` and `coordinator.jsonc`. In headless mode it uses the folder's `brief.md` by default and accepts `PROMPT_FILE` as an override. Each invocation owns a temporary roster and tears down its workers when the session exits. For workers you want to reuse across sessions, use the persistent roster workflow below.

### Persistent roster

Run from the repository root. Create the roster in a directory you own with mode 0700 or stricter.

```bash
run_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/opencode-team.XXXXXXXX)
network="$run_dir/research.json"

make spawn-agent NAME=scout CONFIG=examples/teams/research/scout.jsonc NETWORK="$network"
make spawn-agent NAME=verify CONFIG=examples/teams/research/verify.jsonc NETWORK="$network"

make team-up NETWORK="$network"
# Exit the TUI before starting the headless session below.
make team-up NETWORK="$network" MODE=run \
  PROMPT_FILE=examples/teams/research/brief.md > answer.md

make team-down NETWORK="$network"
```

The launcher gives each worker a private workspace and HOME/XDG paths. It passes your native profile unchanged via `OPENCODE_CONFIG`. A sibling prompt can be referenced with `{file:./scout.md}`. For a custom profile that opts into `{file:{env:TEAM_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE}}`, use `SYSTEM_PROMPT=/path/to/prompt.md` or let the launcher use the sibling Markdown file. Configs and any referenced files are trusted inputs.

Team-up checks the roster's worker identities and Agent Cards, then warms one coordinator for those URLs. Workers added during a session become available on the next team-up. Exiting the coordinator leaves the workers up. Team-down checks the saved PID and process start time before signaling each process. If a process cannot be confirmed stopped, the roster retains its record for a retry. The stable lock file remains beside the roster so concurrent commands keep using the same lock. Coordinator state, including receipts and session data, remains in the private runtime directory after shutdown for inspection; it can contain sensitive material. Inspect and reconcile it privately before manually removing it. Folder mode prints the retained private directory.

If a worker fails its startup readiness check, the launcher stops it but retains its private `worker.err` and `ready.jsonl` files and prints their directory for diagnosis. Treat this startup evidence as sensitive; do not publish it raw.

## Receipts and telemetry

When a coordinator exits, the launcher keeps a private (mode 0600) copy of its bridge `receipts.jsonl` as `.test-results/teams/<UTC timestamp>-<random>.jsonl`, in both folder and roster mode, so it survives `team-down` and temporary-folder cleanup. The copy is never overwritten and a failed copy only prints a warning. Receipts hold task and context IDs (raw in results) and call metadata, no prompt text, so treat them as private; the report prints only counts, tool names, states and timings.

```bash
make team-report FILE=.test-results/teams/<name>.jsonl
```

The report is one `jq` script (`examples/teams/report.jq`). It prints calls per tool and peer, call-to-result durations, polls (`a2a_get_task`) per task, send-to-completed time per task, rejections by tool and reason, and attempts per bridge connection against the 40-call ceiling. Task numbers follow first submission time, and each final state is selected by the latest result timestamp. Tasks and connections are numbered instead of printing IDs; peers appear only as loopback `host:port`. Use it as a check, not enforcement: nothing stops a coordinator from exceeding its budget.

## Golden user journey

Use the research team for the walkthrough. Start both workers in one shell, open OpenCode, ask for three changes backed by the official release notes, then exit the TUI. Reuse those workers for the headless brief and shut down the roster. The ports below are illustrative. Use the endpoints your workers print.

```text
$ make spawn-agent NAME=scout CONFIG=examples/teams/research/scout.jsonc NETWORK="$network"
  ready      scout · http://127.0.0.1:41321/
  roster     research.json · workers 1

$ make spawn-agent NAME=verify CONFIG=examples/teams/research/verify.jsonc NETWORK="$network"
  ready      verify · http://127.0.0.1:41322/
  roster     research.json · workers 2

$ make team-up NETWORK="$network"
  registered scout · http://127.0.0.1:41321/
  registered verify · http://127.0.0.1:41322/
  ready      coordinator · 2 workers · http://127.0.0.1:41323
  opening    OpenCode TUI
```

In OpenCode, ask “Have scout find the latest stable Node.js release notes. Give the official URL to verify and ask for three documented changes. Cite the source.” Look for both calls in OpenCode’s tool activity and check that the answer cites the original release notes. Exit the TUI to return to the shell.

```text
$ make team-up NETWORK="$network" MODE=run PROMPT_FILE=examples/teams/research/brief.md > answer.md
  registered scout · http://127.0.0.1:41321/
  registered verify · http://127.0.0.1:41322/
  ready      coordinator · 2 workers · http://127.0.0.1:41324

$ make team-down NETWORK="$network"
  stopped    scout
  stopped    verify
  stopped    research.json · roster removed
```

### Terminal presentation

- Keep a single aligned status column and use short, lowercase verbs such as `ready`, `registered`, `opening`, and `stopped`. Put the worker name and endpoint on the same line. Keep ports and paths easy to copy.
- Use one accent on the status label when stderr is a terminal. Honor `NO_COLOR`, keep redirected output plain, and make every status understandable from its text alone.
- Keep launcher status on stderr. In headless mode, stdout is the coordinator's answer, so `> answer.md` captures clean Markdown. Let the native OpenCode TUI show tool activity and the response.
- Announce readiness after its check passes. Announce worker completion only when the corresponding A2A task outcome has been observed. For a failure, name the affected worker or service and give the next action, such as retrying `team-down` for a retained process record.
- Review the transcript in a narrow terminal, with `NO_COLOR=1`, and with stdout redirected. Confirm that the operator can see which workers joined, when OpenCode is ready, and whether teardown finished.

# Architecture and scope

## Goal

Expose OpenCode as a small A2A agent while keeping OpenCode's ACP subprocess as the authority for coding-session behavior. The A2A server owns the external task boundary; an adapter translates task input into ACP session/prompt operations and translates ACP updates into A2A events.

```text
A2A client
  -> A2A v1 JSON-RPC + Agent Card (HTTP)
  -> A2A request handler / task store
  -> executor and ACP adapter
  -> OpenCode subprocess (ACP NDJSON over stdin/stdout)
```

Keep protocol responsibilities at their boundary: A2A task IDs and lifecycle belong to A2A; session IDs, prompt turns, permission requests and session updates belong to ACP. Do not treat the HTTP admission response as completion of the underlying OpenCode work.

## Contract decisions

- **A2A:** use the current JavaScript SDK v1 server composition (`AgentExecutor`, `DefaultRequestHandler`, task store, `AgentEvent` helpers, and Express JSON-RPC / Agent Card handlers). Declare only capabilities actually implemented. SDK sample: [A2A JS sample server](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-js/blob/main/src/samples/agents/sample-agent/index.ts); [migration guide](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-js/blob/main/docs/migration-guide.md).
- **ACP v1:** run the OpenCode executable as a subprocess using newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout; stdout is protocol-only and stderr is the logging channel. Supply an absolute working directory. The reviewed OpenCode 2.2.7 executable retains ACP protocol version 1, `session/new`, `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, updates, and permission callbacks; see [runtime compatibility evidence](/docs/opencode-runtime-upgrade.md). See [ACP v1 initialization](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/initialization), [session setup](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/session-setup), [prompt turn](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/prompt-turn), [cancellation](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/cancellation), and [OpenCode ACP docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/acp).
- **Turn completion:** ACP v1 `session/prompt` returns `PromptResponse.stopReason`. Use the response for that prompt as the authoritative completion signal, not a quiet stream or unrelated event. The MVP policy treats only `end_turn` as successful; explicitly map other defined stop reasons to truthful non-success outcomes. [ACP v1 prompt turn](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/prompt-turn).
- **Correlation:** retain explicit mapping between A2A task, ACP session, and in-flight prompt. In the existing fork HTTP V2 probe, admission/delivery IDs did not correlate later assistant/terminal events; they are not substitutes for protocol task/session correlation. Treat that observation as fork-specific evidence, not a general protocol rule.

## Project policy (not protocol requirements)

Keep v1 scope narrow: map each A2A context to one ACP session in memory, reuse it for follow-up tasks while the gateway is running, and admit only one active prompt globally. Bound the number of sessions; restart recovery is unsupported. Deny unsupported interactive permission requests rather than silently approving them, and advertise only implemented capabilities in the Agent Card. These are implementation choices, not mandates imposed by ACP or A2A.

## Implementation boundaries

- `server.ts` composes the SDK, gates readiness on ACP, preserves explicit context intent through public SDK methods, and owns HTTP shutdown.
- `executor.ts` holds the bounded context map and single admission slot, publishes task/working/artifact/terminal events, and uses the prompt response as its outcome.
- `acp-client.ts` owns the pinned subprocess, persistent stable-v1 connection, update filtering, permission denial, deadlines and process cleanup. It never retries an uncertain prompt.
- `request-handler.ts` keeps the SDK's `InMemoryTaskStore` but synchronizes cancellation with its original event consumer; this avoids SDK 1.3 duplicate artifact persistence. This narrow workaround is regression-tested, not a second task database.

The cancellation adapter depends on the original SDK persistence consumer staying
alive. Explicitly closing the public SDK stream generator is distinct from an
HTTP client disconnect and is not a supported takeover mechanism. See
[SDK cancellation evidence](/docs/sdk-cancellation.md) before changing the
adapter or the transport's stream-consumption lifecycle.

## Deliberately unsupported

OpenCode HTTP adapters, ACP v2, rich file/image inputs, reasoning/tool output, interactive permission/forms, request-scoped models or workspaces, parallel prompts, authentication/multi-tenancy, push notifications, outbound A2A, durable task/session recovery, replay, databases and distributed scheduling. The existing Python fork is unchanged. The loopback listener is for an operator-controlled trusted workspace, not an untrusted public endpoint.

# Bun runtime security

Tracking: [issue #60](https://github.com/tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite/issues/60).

## Runtime decision and security boundary

Pin the standalone Bun executable to **1.4.4**, the first patched release for
[GHSA-26q8-h657-pf84](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/security/advisories/GHSA-26q8-h657-pf84).
The previous 1.3.9 pin is affected. This records exposure, not observed exploitation.
`@types/bun` is a development declaration package, not the executable runtime.
The dependency versions and frozen lockfile do not need changing for this pin.

Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys were compromised; six issue TLS certificates.
Bun 1.4.4 removes three emSign roots, updates its bundle to NSS 3.131.1, and rejects
chains containing the compromised public keys with `CERT_REVOKED`. Key-based
rejection also covers cross-signed intermediates and explicitly supplied CAs.
The exposure includes outbound `fetch`, package downloads through `bun install`
and `bunx`, and other TLS APIs; a loopback-only inbound listener does not repair it.

OS CA updates, `--use-system-ca`, and `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` alone do **not** repair
affected Bun releases: system certificates are added to the bundled store, not
used instead of it. Explicit per-connection CA lists can replace the default
store, but are not a process-wide repair. Do not disable certificate validation.

OpenCode is a separate executable/runtime boundary. Replacing standalone Bun does
not replace an embedded runtime in OpenCode; that assessment is tracked in
[issue #61](https://github.com/tbrandenburg/opencode-a2a-lite/issues/61).
The SDK cancellation adapter and its [independent removal gate](/docs/sdk-cancellation.md)
are unchanged.

after `closeAllConnections()` without calling `server.close()`. This relied on
Bun 1.3.9 closing the listener as a side effect. A provider-free minimal probe:

```sh

  const server = createServer((_request, response) => response.end("ok"));
  await new Promise(resolve => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
  const closed = new Promise(resolve => server.once("close", () => resolve("closed")));
  server.closeAllConnections();
  const outcome = await Promise.race([closed, Bun.sleep(200).then(() => "still-open")]);
  console.log(JSON.stringify({bun: Bun.version, outcome, listening: server.listening}));
  if (server.listening) await new Promise(resolve => server.close(resolve));
'
```

`make release` tags/pushes and creates a GitHub release; it does **not** publish npm.

provider keys, private prompts, reasoning, or raw peer logs into commands/release
notes. Do not add registry credentials to the repository.

## 1. Contract and prerequisites

```bash
        "per_connection": [{"connection_index": index,
```

# Passive supervision for the pipeline smoke

This is the infrastructure-only watchdog for the
[two-worker bootstrap](/docs/manual-two-worker-pipeline.md#6-supervise-and-run-once).
Review this file, then copy its single Python block into the owned `STATE/watchdog.py`.
It reads the existing guard's metadata receipts and signals only the owned resources
through `STATE/cleanup.sh`. It makes no MCP/A2A/ACP calls, chooses no stage or peer,
generates no prompt, and scores no answer. It is not a topology runner.

## Contents

- [Inputs and limits](#inputs-and-limits)
- [Watchdog](#watchdog)
- [Interpretation](#interpretation)

## Inputs and limits

Use a fresh private state directory. Start after same-server warmup but before the
model client. The bootstrap supplies `mcp-receipts.jsonl`, PID files, `cleanup.sh`,
and `client.exit`. Never reuse prior receipts, handles, or connections. The watchdog
uses the runbook's 30-second submit-plus-wait deadline, eight polls per task, and
32-attempt ordinary-work detection threshold (eight of 40 reserved), and at most two submissions.
The submission cap does not choose peers or enforce a stage order. Its separate 180-second
invocation safety cutoff does not extend an operation's deadline.

This is passive observation every 50ms, not a pre-dispatch quota guard. Concurrent
calls can pass the threshold before shutdown, and processing stops at the first
violation. `observed_attempts_at_stop` is only that processed prefix, never the final
attempt count. The existing endpoint guard forwards at most 40 tool requests per
connection; subsequent attempts are locally denied but still count as attempts.
It therefore does not hard-stop the caller itself at 40 attempts.
If the required gate is prevention before dispatch at either limit, this recipe is
unsupported: record BLOCKED **before submission**, not an enforcement claim.
The endpoint guard separately denies `a2a_send_message` unless its top-level
`blocking` value is literal `false`; this mode policy is enforced before forwarding.
Rejected attempts still count toward the 40-attempt limit and are observed in
sanitized receipts. The 32-call threshold, deadlines and polling cadence remain
passive/operator supervision, not pre-dispatch enforcement.

Each accepted send has its own monotonic cutoff mapped from its timestamped guard
receipt. A result arriving after the cutoff fails even if the task completed.
Pending/uncertain operations remain pending/uncertain when owned cleanup interrupts
them; process shutdown is not evidence of remote cancellation.

```python
    try:

    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):

                    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=45)

            stop("missing-request-binding")
        key = str(row["id"])
        if event == "call":
            requests[key] = row
            if row["tool"] == "a2a_send_streaming":
                stop("unexpected-streaming-submission")
            if row["tool"] == "a2a_cancel_task":
                stop("unexpected-cancellation-attempt")
            if row["tool"] == "a2a_send_message":
                active[key] = {"deadline": moment(row) + 30, "peer": row.get("peer")}
                submissions += 1
                if submissions > 2:
                    stop("submission-cap")
                if row.get("blocking") is not False:
                    stop("nonblocking-contract")
                if row.get("contextPresent") or row.get("taskPresent"):
                    stop("unexpected-continuation")
            if row["tool"] == "a2a_get_task":
                handle = (row.get("peer"), row.get("taskHash"))
                if not any(item.get("handle") == handle for item in active.values()):
                    stop("unbound-task-poll")
                if handle in observing:
                    stop("overlapping-task-polls")
                observing.add(handle)
                polls[handle] = polls.get(handle, 0) + 1
                if polls[handle] > 8:
                    stop("poll-cap")
            continue
        call = requests.pop(key, None)
        if call is None or call["tool"] != row.get("tool"):
            stop("unpaired-result")
        if row.get("ok") is not True:
            stop("tool-error-or-uncertain-submit")
        pending = key if call["tool"] == "a2a_send_message" else None
        if pending is not None:
            if not all(isinstance(row.get(name), str) and row[name] for name in ("taskId", "contextId")):
                stop("missing-returned-handle")
            digest = hashlib.sha256(row["taskId"].encode()).hexdigest()
            active[pending]["handle"] = (call.get("peer"), digest)
        if call["tool"] == "a2a_get_task":
            handle = (call.get("peer"), call.get("taskHash"))
            observing.discard(handle)
            pending = next((name for name, item in active.items()
                            if item.get("handle") == handle), None)
        if pending is not None:
            if moment(row) > active[pending]["deadline"]:
                stop("late-operation-result")
            if row.get("state") == "TASK_STATE_COMPLETED":
                del active[pending]
            elif row.get("state") != "TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED" and row.get("state") != "TASK_STATE_WORKING":
                stop("task-not-completed")
            elif call["tool"] == "a2a_get_task" and polls[handle] == 8:
                stop("poll-cap-with-pending-task")
    if any(time.monotonic() >= item["deadline"] for item in active.values()):
        stop("absolute-operation-deadline")
    if (root / "client.exit").exists():
        if active or requests:
            stop("client-ended-with-pending-evidence")
        try:
            (root / "supervision.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                "interrupted": False, "pending": 0, "observed_attempts_at_stop": attempts,
            }))
        except OSError:
            stop("supervision-report-error")
        break
    if time.monotonic() - started >= 180:
        stop("invocation-safety-cutoff")
    time.sleep(0.05)
```

## Interpretation

Require `interrupted:false` and `pending:0` for the supervision gate. This does not
prove two stages ran, inputs/artifacts matched, or a marker was correct: the executing
agent must inspect the actual sessions and paired receipts separately. No numeric
minimum poll gap is invented here; timestamps are retained and overlapping requests
for the same task fail. The model still owns polling decisions under the prompt's
spaced-poll instruction; publish observed gaps, never claim a prompt enforces time.

After the coordinator/MCP connection and receipt writers have exited, reconcile the
**complete final** receipt stream using the bootstrap's read-only final-count query.
Count `call` plus `rejected` per connection and across the run, including records
after the watchdog's processed prefix. A final total **>32 fails the reserve gate**;
**>40 also fails the overall-attempt gate**. Exactly 32 triggers passive shutdown
without itself proving a reserve overrun. Missing, malformed or trailing incomplete
receipts make reconciliation INCOMPLETE. Reconcile calls/results separately by
connection, MCP ID and tool: missing results remain missing/uncertain, not canceled,
even when the final count is within budget. Inspection must not reopen MCP; count
again after any standalone inspection to include its connection receipts.

An interruption is a supervision/caller/evidence finding, not automatically an
adapter defect. Preserve the private state and returned handles for review, execute
the bootstrap's remaining cleanup checks, and stop without another model attempt.

## Generator lifetime is not HTTP connection lifetime

There are three different boundaries, exercised separately:

1. **Explicit public-generator `return()`:** SDK `sendMessageStream` stops its
   event queue in `finally`. That generator was the original persistence owner.
   After saving `A`, closing it, and then canceling, the adapter has no consumer
   left to save `B`, `B`, the empty final append, or the terminal event. Cancellation
   rejects at the adapter deadline; `GetTask` stays working with only `A`. The
   stock SDK's extra cancellation consumer happens to take over in this case.
   This is a known limitation, not a supported recovery path or a false success.
2. **Paused public-generator iteration:** events remain queued, but persistence
   waits for the next iteration. Resuming within the adapter deadline lets the
   original owner persist the exact artifact and cancel successfully. A client
   that holds the generator paused indefinitely cannot expect cancellation to
   finish successfully through this adapter.
3. **Real JSON-RPC HTTP disconnect/paused socket reads:** the current Express SDK
   loop continues iterating and calling `response.write`; it does not explicitly
   close the generator on disconnect or await write backpressure. The new real
   HTTP probes destroy a response socket after `A`, or pause the response before
   a 4 MiB repeated-chunk burst. Cancellation still reaches the truthful terminal
   save while reads are paused. Resuming a connected reader yields text identical
   to storage, including the empty `lastChunk` append.

The HTTP probes use an actual ACP subprocess, gateway, SDK middleware and TCP
connection, with an atomically allocated ephemeral loopback port. They do not
mock execution or call generator `return()` as a substitute for disconnect.
They cover canceled-winning and completed-winning outcomes. A paused socket and
large response do not prove a particular kernel buffer threshold or bounded
memory usage on every platform. These tests are **not** a general backpressure
or resource-exhaustion guarantee. A future transport that closes or stops driving
the generator must re-evaluate persistence ownership before adopting that change.

An upstream fix needs one persistence owner independent of generator lifetime,
or a safe takeover after closure without simultaneous append writers. Merely
deleting the cancellation ResultManager does not solve both boundaries.

```ts
if (submitted.outcome === "uncertain") {
  // The request may have been accepted. No handle was received. Do not resend.
  return submitted;
}
const observed = await peer.wait(submitted, options);
// Persist/retain observed.handle in the caller, even if observed is pending.
// For a new turn, choose a new local deadline, and pass observed.handle to submit.
```

Deadlines are **absolute monotonic `performance.now()` milliseconds**, not epoch
timestamps. Submission and waiting share one deadline when they are one operation.
Each MCP call uses an abort signal with a timer for the remaining local deadline;
progress cannot extend it. The SDK request timer is a maximum-duration fallback,
not the local deadline, and no maximum total timeout is configured. Every polling
sleep is capped by the remaining time and abortable. No new poll starts after
deadline/abort. Event-loop scheduling still has bounded test headroom; JavaScript
cannot interrupt a blocked event loop.

The immutable handle contains the **actual** peer URL, context ID and task ID.
Follow-up submissions send `context_id`, omit `task_id` and request nonblocking
execution. Each turn gets a distinct task ID. A helper bound to another peer
rejects the handle locally. Unknown/expired contexts fail remotely; the helper
does not omit the context and silently restart the conversation.

`Observation.task` uses the pinned official A2A SDK decoder (numeric SDK state
enum and decoded parts). `payloadText` accepts both decoded and wire task parts.
`outcome` distinguishes `completed`, `failed` (including rejected), `canceled` and
`pending` (including interrupted/input-required work). MCP tool success is not
evidence of task completion. Malformed results fail validation.

## Stop waiting is not cancel work

- A local wait returns `pending` with `reason: deadline | aborted | poll-limit |
  budget`, its retained handle and last observed task. The remote task may have
  progressed since that observation. No automatic remote cancellation occurs.
- A timed-out, aborted or disconnected **submission** without a received handle
  returns `uncertain` and its cause, without invented identifiers. No resend or
  background recovery is attempted. Submission tool errors remain visible in
  `cause` too: a bridge error, including its own unary timeout, does not prove that
  the peer never accepted the request. This is intentionally conservative.
- `peer.get(handle, newOptions)` can inspect a task after a local wait expires.
  `peer.cancel(handle, newOptions)` is a **separate explicit remote operation**.
  Use a fresh deadline/signal and keep the MCP connection open for intervention.
- Cancel returns the actual observed outcome, not a promised `canceled` label.
  Cancel errors and unknown-task errors propagate; the caller retains its handle.
  In a losing race, this gateway can report “ACP did not cancel the task” while a
  subsequent `get` reports `completed`. Do not retry cancellation automatically.
- MCP abort sends a request-cancellation notification; that is not proof of A2A
  cancellation. Lifecycle shutdown closes the connection/resources, unlike a
  per-operation signal, and therefore prevents further calls on that connection.

Polling defaults to eight attempts, spaced across the remaining deadline. A
caller may select at most 24 polls, but the helper stops with eight calls remaining
on the connection for intervention/final verification. The existing guard still
caps attempted calls at 40. Discovery and other `connection.call` requests count
against that same local budget. Do not bypass accounting with raw
`connection.client.callTool`, increase the guard budget, or reconnect to evade it.
`stopWhen` permits a bounded partial-output probe without waiting for completion.

## Bridge pin and coordinator guidance

Bridge 4.0.2's unary peer budget is 60 seconds; the gateway default prompt budget
is 120 seconds. Prefer nonblocking send plus bounded task polling for longer work,
not a 150-second blocking MCP call. Polling is **not SSE streaming**.

This project's endpoint guard requires the literal boolean `blocking: false` on
`a2a_send_message`; omitted, true, or mistyped values are denied before forwarding.
This is an optional-guard policy, not a change to the bridge or A2A protocol. Poll
`a2a_get_task` using the actual returned peer/task/context handles until a terminal
state is observed; for continuation reuse the actual `context_id` and omit the old
`task_id`. A local timeout or abort is not remote cancellation; a submission that
times out without a handle remains uncertain and must not be resent.

The pinned `a2a_send_streaming` schema has no `context_id`. The helper exposes nonblocking submission plus polling only; it does not
accept a streaming mode option. Use polling for continuation. Fresh-context direct
streaming remains available through the existing raw tool. Actual streaming
continuation needs a separately reviewed upstream schema and pin change.

**This host helper does not govern the model's direct MCP tool calls.** Equivalent
coordinator instructions must tell the model to retain returned peer/context/task
IDs, send `a2a_send_message` with literal `blocking:false`, continue with the actual
`context_id` but no old `task_id`,
inspect task state rather than MCP success, reserve intervention calls, and treat
local timeouts as pending/uncertain rather than canceled. Neither those instructions
nor the helper change gateway concurrency/security semantics. The guard enforces
the 40-attempt cap, not the eight-call reserve; direct model calls need independently
observed bounds/reserve and cannot inherit this helper's clock or polling sleeps.

   select a favorite before the judge sees the inputs.
5. Observe the judge's actual terminal task and stored artifact. Report missing
   proposals or integrity uncertainty explicitly rather than attributing them to
   judge reasoning. Stop after the predeclared comparison.

## Coordinator prompt sketch

> Collect independent proposals using fresh nonblocking tasks. Keep source handles
> separate. Once the required proposals are completed, give J their exact original
> artifacts, separately labeled. Poll J's actual returned handle and stop. Do not
> substitute summaries, invent a vote, or resend uncertain proposals.

## Verify and bound

Correlate each proposal artifact with the judge's received input, including nested
strings or formatting when exact text is required. Distinguish tool-argument changes
from transport changes. Receiving intact inputs does not establish a good selection,
and a small proposer set does not establish larger fan-in capacity or reliability.

## Control and inputs

Let selected worker sessions call reviewed peer workers through their own local
guards. Treat the allowed graph as permissions, not a requirement to exercise every
edge. Obtain an exact non-self peer set per caller, one finite delegation-wave rule,
an explicit no-forwarding rule for recipients, and independently supervised budgets.

## Procedure

1. Review temporary worker-side agent permissions and each exact non-self peer guard.
   Do not add production delegation support or broaden peers to obtain a result.
2. Verify tools on the actual initiating worker server, not just the coordinator's
   catalog. Confirm recipient behavior forbids recursive fanback or another wave.
3. Have the coordinator seed the reviewed root worker with one bounded task. Begin
   with one useful approved worker-originated edge rather than a whole-graph sweep.
4. Have the initiating worker discover/verify its intended peer, explicitly submit
   one nonblocking fresh-context task, retain the returned binding, and poll that
   task under both local and ancestor limits. The recipient does not delegate further.
5. Return the observed completed peer artifact through the initiating worker's root
   result. Have the coordinator inspect that root task's actual terminal artifact.
6. Stop after the approved wave. Any additional edge needs an explicit finite scope
   and remaining supervised budget; never reconnect to reset a connection's count.

## Root prompt sketch

> Make one reviewed peer call through your own guarded tools, explicitly nonblocking.
> The recipient must answer without delegation. Keep the actual peer/context/task
> binding, collect the completed artifact, and return it through your root task.
> No self-call, recursion, fanback, repeat wave, guessed handle or uncertain resend.

## Verify and bound

Inspect the worker-originated call in the initiating worker's session; coordinator
calls to the same recipient do not substitute for it. Correlate actual inputs and
artifacts at each gateway and enforce budgets per connection, not just a global
total. One observed edge is not evidence that the whole mesh, cycles, or other
workers' delegation works. Missing worker tools are an execution-layer blocker,
not by themselves evidence of an A2A adapter defect.

   Use the host's reviewed read-only probes; do not warm a separate inspection server
   and assume the ACP session uses its tool registry.
3. Submit one fresh root task nonblocking. Include the explicit nonblocking argument
   requirement in the instructions every parent will receive and forward to its child.
   Prohibit self-calls, broader peers, unapproved descendants and uncertain resubmits.

   poll it to terminal completion, and return the actual stored child artifact. Limit
   the initial probe to a useful approved path; do not expand just to fill the diagram.
5. Independently supervise each child operation and its ancestors. Child deadlines
   must fit inside the remaining parent deadline, not restart or extend it. Count
   calls separately on every worker connection and preserve each reserve.
6. Require the coordinator to observe the root task's terminal state and artifact.

> Use only your reviewed child peers, at most the approved depth. Explicitly select

child input, and completed artifact separately. Text that resembles a tool call is
not a call. Keep root polling count and elapsed time distinct: do not stop early
under an invented cap or extend the deadline to compensate. Report pending/uncertain
outcomes honestly. A successful path is not a balanced-tree or reliability result.

parallelism with observed overlap. Verify each input and stored artifact against
